key_insight: AA-ViT aims to generate contrast-enhanced brain MRI from non-contrast scans by making the vision transformer anatomically aware. It combines structural and frequency guidance so the model can better preserve brain anatomy while improving lesion visibility.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the difficulty of synthesizing high-quality contrast-enhanced brain MRI when contrast agents cannot be used or are risky for certain patients. The goal is to improve tumour localization and diagnostic visibility without relying on chemical contrast injection.
method: Uses an anatomically aware Vision Transformer to model brain MRI more faithfully than generic image synthesis approaches.
Incorporates structural guidance to preserve anatomical boundaries and spatial consistency in synthesized images.
Adds frequency guidance to capture fine texture and contrast details that are important for lesion enhancement.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work shows how domain knowledge can be built into transformer-based generative models for medical imaging. It highlights a path toward safer, more clinically useful image synthesis systems that support diagnosis when contrast agents are not an option.

paper_title: AA-ViT: Anatomically Aware Vision Transformer with Structural and Frequency Guidance for Contrast Enhanced Brain MRI Synthesis
paper_authors: Talha Meraj, Tom Flannery, Charlie Cummins, Matt Townend, Thomas C Booth
